On the evidence I have seen from the three inquests referred to, the Royal Berkshire Hospital's death investigation process is not working well.
I have seen evidence of delayed morbidity and mortality meetings with no clear system for ensuring that these discussions happen timeously.
There is little (if any) record of areas of concern identified at meetings - whether at morbidity and mortality meetings or clinical governance meetings.
There is delayed escalation of concerns.
Structured judgement reviews I have reviewed are at best, poor, and at worst, defensive.

Delayed or no scrutiny of cases being reported to the coroner because the cause of death is unnatural, given that medical examiners are not funded to scrutinise those cases. Opportunities for early learning are therefore being lost.

On 25 April 2022 this second SATS machine, stopped working. It had some sort of error message on the screen. The parents contacted the community nurse team and Devon's mother had to attend the hospital that night to pick up a new SATS machine.

If a safety plan is put in place which includes the use of a SATS machine to monitor the wellbeing of the patient, and that machine is less than at least 99% reliable, or has software issues, or is unsuitable for home use, or is complicated to use, this may result in a false sense of security from the family who will rely on the machine to alert them if the oxygen levels drop below a certain figure.
